title: Integrated Signal Triage and Vertical Opportunity Sizing Playbook for Model Landscape Tracking
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Goal: produce a repeatable playbook that synthesizes heterogeneous signals (public model releases, benchmark regressions, pricing shifts, partner/infra announcements, and R&D teasers) into prioritized vertical opportunity sizing and procurement timing recommendations for Redwood sales and product strategy.

Scope:
- Define signal taxonomy (capability, cost, latency, licensing, quantization readiness, regional availability).
- Establish signal ingestion cadence (real-time feeds, weekly syntheses, ad-hoc deep dives).
- Map signals to verticals (finserv, healthcare, edtech, search/knowledge work) with rough TAM and adoption friction estimates.
- Produce a decision rubric for when to: (a) onboard a model variant to hosted catalog, (b) recommend Dedicated capacity sizing, (c) flag for Private/VPC pilot.
- Deliverables: one-page playbook, 12-slide executive brief, spreadsheet with signal->vertical mapping and scoring, and a lightweight alerting spec for Console team.
success_metrics: Playbook approved by GTM and Eng leadership by due_date
Operational signal pipeline prototype running weekly (ingest + synth)
Top-3 vertical opportunity recommendations with TAM and recommended go/no-go within playbook
>30% reduction in time-to-decision for model onboarding requests measured in follow-ups
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc published to Confluence with reviewer comments addressed
Signal taxonomy implemented as a spreadsheet + mapping columns and documented parsers
One pilot vertical (e.g., SMB search) has a scored recommendation and next-step plan
Alerting spec handed to Console PM with mockups and ingestion endpoints
approach_summary: We will combine automated public-signal scraping (model release notes, papers, vendor pricing updates), partner channel intel (sales/solutions feedback), and periodic benchmark sweeps (latency/cost on representative queries). Each signal gets normalized into a small feature set and a human-reviewed score. Scores are aggregated into vertical-fit scores using weighted heuristics; weights are tunable and documented. The playbook emphasizes reproducibility and handoffs: PM produces strategy recommendations, Eng prototypes ingestion, Console picks up alerting spec, GTM validates customer demand signals.
key_tradeoffs: Breadth vs depth: wide coverage of many models reduces sensitivity; focused vertical probes provide higher confidence but cost more time
Realtime alerts vs weekly synthesis: realtime increases noise; weekly syntheses are calmer but may miss rapid supplier changes
Automation vs human review: automated scoring accelerates scale but requires curated thresholds to prevent false positives that waste Eng/GTM bandwidth
data_sources: Model release RSS and GitHub repos (paper/model tags)
Public benchmark corpora (Hugging Face leaderboards, Eleuther benchmarks)
Vendor pricing pages and cloud instance SKU monitors
Sales CRM notes (redacted), partner channel reports
risks_and_mitigations: Signal noise / false positives -> mitigation: human-in-the-loop verification step for any change that would trigger onboarding or capacity commits
Incomplete pricing transparency -> mitigation: model cost placeholder with sensitivity ranges and flagged unknowns
Data privacy for CRM signals -> mitigation: anonymize inputs and only surface aggregated demand signals to playbook outputs
